clue.text: It was fired in church, in a Derbyshire town

indicators.note: the church is placed in the town, so the town's letters are opened up around it

parts.note: Matlock is the county town of Derbyshire, in England's Peak District

explanation.surface: Someone fires a gun inside a church in a quiet Derbyshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is a link; the second, 'in a Derbyshire town', puts CH inside MATLOCK. 'It was fired' reads as part of the story but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An early musket whose powder was ignited by a slow-burning match, so it was a gun that was fired.

clue.text: Means arranged for girl to span ravine

indicators.note: the girl's name stretches across the ravine like a bridge, so it goes around it

parts.note: Mary is a girl's name
a chine is a deep narrow ravine, a word used on the Isle of Wight and in Dorset

explanation.surface: A plan is devised for a girl to be bridged across a ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: CHINE is a regional English word for a ravine cut by a stream to the sea; MARY goes round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Machinery is the organised system by which something is done, as in the machinery of government.

clue.text: Discrimination, in Baptista's terminology

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across these two words

explanation.surface: A remark about the way Baptista, a character in The Taming of the Shrew, uses words to show fine judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the end of BaptisTA'S and continues into TErminology.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste is fine judgement in matters of style, the faculty of telling good from bad.

clue.text: Rashly cure about 500 on 3rd of August

indicators.note: the word for cure goes about, that is around, the Roman numeral

parts.note: to cure is to heal
D is the Roman numeral for 500

indicators.note: only the third letter of the word August is taken

explanation.surface: Someone rashly hopes for a cure costing about 500 on the third of August.
explanation.definitionFit: To act headlong is to act hastily and without thinking.

clue.text: The gall, wearing this on the king's birthday!

definitions.text: wearing this on the king's birthday!

explanation.surface: A cheeky courtier wears something impudent on the monarch's birthday.
explanation.walkthrough: Oak Apple Day, 29 May, celebrated the birthday and Restoration of Charles II, who hid in an oak tree; people wore oak apples or oak leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: An oak apple is a growth on an oak caused by a wasp, and it was worn on Royal Oak Day, the restored monarch's birthday.

clue.text: Having been cured, he, sleeps, apparently

explanation.surface: A man recovered from illness who now seems to spend his time asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cured' suggests recovery from illness, but it means smoked and salted, and 'he' is the male fish; 'kip' is British slang for sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoked herring is one sense; someone who kips, or naps, is the other.

clue.text: About to steal from its branches?

definitions.text: About to steal from its branches?

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about
to steal is to rob

explanation.surface: Someone is about to pinch fruit from a tree's branches.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes picking the pods of this tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The carob is a Mediterranean tree whose sweet pods hang from its branches, ripe for taking.

clue.text: Youngsters backing some of our members

explanation.surface: Young people are supporting some members of our club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like support, but the calves are at the back of the legs, our members.
explanation.definitionFit: Young cattle are one sense; the fleshy rear parts of our lower legs, limbs being members, are the other.

clue.text: Priest's office delivers reprimand about man's execution

indicators.note: the word for reprimand goes about, that is around, the beheaded man

parts.note: to rate is an old word for to scold or reprimand

indicators.note: an execution here is a beheading, so the man loses his head, his first letter

parts.note: Hector is a man's name

explanation.surface: A priest's office sends a rebuke over a man being put to death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Execution' cuts the head off HECTOR, leaving ECTOR, which 'about' puts inside RATE; 'delivers' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectorate is the position or term held by a rector, a parish priest.

clue.text: Scholar raised equipment for -making printed material.

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a scholar

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word is read from the bottom up, so backwards

parts.note: kit is equipment

explanation.surface: A scholar lifts up the gear used for producing printed fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' reverses KIT to TIK in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Batik is cloth patterned by wax-resist dyeing, an Indonesian printing technique.

clue.text: Bird seen around ship — a Ukrainian rider

indicators.note: the bird's letters go around the ship and the a

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A bird is spotted circling a ship, then a horseman from Ukraine.
explanation.definitionFit: Cossacks were horsemen of the Ukrainian and Russian steppes, famed cavalry.

clue.text: European jazz enthusiast raises a frightful stink

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the animal noted for doing so

parts.note: a Pole is a European
cat is old jazz slang for a fan

explanation.surface: A European jazz fan makes a terrible fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raises a stink' suggests a complaint, but the definition describes the smell of the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The polecat, a weasel relative, gives off a foul smell when threatened.

clue.text: Model 23 ac from a supplier of hands

definitions.text: 23 ac from a supplier of hands

explanation.surface: A model statement made by a card dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 across is ASSERTION; a card dealer, who supplies hands, would say 'I deal'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a perfect example to copy; the dealer's claim 'I deal' is the other reading.

clue.text: Sounds like a conciliation job — paid for by results

indicators.note: the clue says outright that the phrase is spoken, so the letters entered are those of a same-sounding word

parts.note: making peace is a peace work

explanation.surface: A peacemaking task whose pay depends on how well it turns out.
explanation.definitionFit: Piecework is labour paid by the number of items produced, not by the hour.

clue.text: Ravel, unusually lean gent!

indicators.note: the letters of lean gent are set out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Someone calls out a thin gentleman by name, perhaps addressing the composer Ravel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ravel' looks like the French composer but is the verb meaning tangle.
explanation.definitionFit: To ravel is to tangle or twist threads together into knots.

clue.text: Changes headgear at entrance to fair-ground?

parts.note: changes is to turns, as in the weather turns
tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: Someone swaps hats on arriving at a funfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At' is a link. TILE is a dated British slang word for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolving gate that admits one person at a time, as at the gate of a sports ground or fair.

clue.text: Prize to conceal in the hand

explanation.surface: Someone hides a trophy in their hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A palm is a symbol of victory, so a prize; to palm a card is a conjuror's hiding it in the hand.

clue.text: She put together a garland most of one

parts.note: to put together is to make, here made
a lei is a Hawaiian flower garland

indicators.note: most of the word means it loses one letter, its first

explanation.surface: A woman has assembled a flower garland, nearly a single one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops the O of ONE, leaving NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeleine is a woman's name, so a she.

clue.text: A northern writer in a western state, sustained by his fellows?

indicators.note: the pieces are placed in the state's abbreviation

parts.note: Cal is short for California
a nib is the writing point of a pen

explanation.surface: A northern author living in California is supported by his colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts A, N and NIB inside CAL, after its C. 'Sustained by his fellows' looks like support but means fed on other people.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eater lives on the flesh of his own kind.

clue.text: Place of worship for these bad characters

indicators.note: the letters, or characters, of these bad are to be set in a new order

explanation.surface: A chapel is the place where these wicked people go to pray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad characters' reads as villains, but characters are letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Bethesda is a pool in Jerusalem and a common name for Nonconformist chapels in Wales.

clue.text: New boy rejected this traveller's. tale

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: Ray is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A new boy dismisses a traveller's story.
explanation.definitionFit: A yarn is a long tall story, the kind told by sailors and travellers.

clue.text: Appeasement by bribery in many a strange legend

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals, so many

indicators.note: strange means the letters of legend are put in a strange order

explanation.surface: Many an odd myth tells of paying off enemies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' makes NEGELD from LEGEND; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Danegeld was tax raised to pay off Viking invaders, the classic payment for peace.

clue.text: Coloured drawing of a prisoner eating fish

indicators.note: the prisoner's letters take in, as if eating, the fish

parts.note: a con is a convict
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A picture shows an inmate eating fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A crayon is a stick of coloured wax, and also a picture made with one.

clue.text: But an unmarried girl isn't, surely

definitions.text: But an unmarried girl isn't, surely

parts.words: But an unmarried girl isn't, surely
parts.note: split the word for a wife into two and it seems to claim that a single young woman is one, which she plainly is not

explanation.surface: A protest that a single girl surely isn't something.
explanation.walkthrough: The informal word for a wife splits into an unmarried girl's title plus a verb, a claim the clue denies.
explanation.definitionFit: Missis is a colloquial word for a wife, which an unmarried girl is not.

clue.text: First lock a set-back? What a statement!

indicators.note: set back means the whole phrase is read backwards

parts.note: first is number one, written No. I
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A first lock suffers a setback, and someone exclaims about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set-back' reverses NO I + TRESS + A, giving A SSERT ION; 'What a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An assertion is a firm declaration that something is so.

clue.text: Assists president on way up

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, US president

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word reads from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: St, street, is a way

explanation.surface: Someone helps a president along the road upward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' is a link placing ABE before TS, ST reversed by 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to help or encourage, typically in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Holy books found in male student's lodging-place

indicators.note: the holy books are found in the word for male

parts.note: he is a male
OT, the Old Testament, is the holy books
L is a learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: Bibles are found in a male student's lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for learner, from the L-plates British learner drivers display.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is a place where travellers lodge.

clue.text: A kingdom given to printers?

parts.note: the NGA, National Graphical Association, was the British printers' trade union

explanation.surface: A kingdom is handed over to the printing trade.
explanation.walkthrough: The NGA was the British printers' union; 'given' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is a Pacific island monarchy.

clue.text: Avengers in the Emerald Isle, indeed

parts.note: Erin is a poetic name for Ireland, the Emerald Isle
indeed means yes

explanation.surface: Avengers appear in Ireland, it is true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Erinyes are the Furies of Greek myth, who pursue wrongdoers.

clue.text: Lowly state — one observed in a dog

parts.note: base means low or lowly
NJ is New Jersey, a US state
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A dog is seen in a humble condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Observed in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The basenji is an African hound that does not bark.

clue.text: A novelist mostly lacking-in compassion

indicators.note: mostly means the novelist's name is used minus its last letter

parts.note: Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy

explanation.surface: A writer is said to be largely without compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the final E from STERNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern means severe and harsh, without warmth.

clue.text: Fruit, extremely toothsome, in Mahmud's territory

parts.note: a sultana is a dried grape

indicators.note: extremely means only the extreme, outer letters of toothsome are taken

explanation.surface: Dried fruit, very tasty, is found in Mahmud's land.
explanation.walkthrough: Mahmud is a typical sultan's name, so his land is a sultanate.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultanate is the land ruled by a sultan.
